description: Cross-repo contract for the georeferenced observation envelope POSTed to Factlas at POST /api/v1/observations. Producers (e.g. Eido capture handoffs) must emit exactly this shape; Factlas validates it as ObservationCreate. Changing this file is a cross-repo act: update the canonical copy and ALL vendored copies in the same change set. Additive fields stay within v1; bump version only for breaking shape changes.
auth: Janua bearer (RS256, verified via JWKS). Service principals authenticate with an OAuth2 client_credentials token — Factlas require_user accepts any valid Janua token with a sub.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS84). Always required — it is the observation's representative point, and Factlas derives h3_8 from it even when a full geometry is supplied.

properties.description: Free-form metadata (producer-specific; e.g. eido_id, mesh_url, title, altitude_m)

confidence.description: Producer confidence in the observation itself — not in the accuracy of its georeference, which belongs in geo_anchor.

geometry.description: Optional GeoJSON geometry (Polygon, MultiPolygon or Point, WGS84 / EPSG:4326) giving the observation's EXTENT rather than only its representative point. Added in the 2026-08-04 revision: a property is an extent, and a lat/lon alone is a pin near one. Factlas stores this as the observation's geom when present and falls back to ST_MakePoint(lon, lat) when absent, so producers that only have a point are unaffected. Rings must be explicitly closed (first coordinate repeated as the last). The observation's lat/lon must still be supplied and should fall inside the geometry.

geo_anchor.description: Optional provenance of the georeference — how the location was obtained and how far to trust it. Recognised keys: 'source' (e.g. 'exif', 'dji_srt', 'operator', 'exif+dji_srt'), 'prior_count' (integer — how many source frames carried a fix; a read-proof, so a consumer can distinguish 'no frames had GPS' from 'nothing ever looked'), 'is_georegistered' (boolean — whether the producer's 3D model was actually aligned to those priors, which is distinct from merely having coordinates), 'footprint_kind' (e.g. 'capture_envelope' — what the geometry represents; 'capture_envelope' is the ground area a capture observed, explicitly NOT a cadastral parcel or building outline), 'footprint_area_m2' (number), and 'crs' (default 'EPSG:4326'). Unrecognised keys are permitted and preserved.

vendored_copies.madfam-org/routecraft: packages/integrations/src/factlas/contracts/observation.v1.json (byte-identical) — emits city_lifestyle_index / event_venue / city_event observations (a producer)

notes.additionalProperties: Set to false as the canonical target. Factlas's current Pydantic ObservationCreate IGNORES unknown top-level fields rather than rejecting them, so producers must not rely on extra fields carrying through — nest producer-specific data under `properties`.
notes.provider: Eido emits provider='eido'; RouteCraft emits provider='routecraft'; Factlas's own default is 'api_user'.
notes.h3: Factlas derives observation.h3_8 server-side (real H3, app-layer) from lat/lon — producers do NOT send it (factlas#16).
notes.geometry_vs_lat_lon: lat/lon stay REQUIRED even when geometry is present. They are the representative point used for h3_8, for the entity row, and by consumers that only handle points (the Atlas renders a marker). Sending a geometry whose interior does not contain lat/lon is a producer bug.
notes.confidence_vs_geo_anchor: `confidence` is confidence in the observation (is this really a warehouse?). Georeference quality — how the position was derived and whether a model was aligned to it — belongs in `geo_anchor`. Conflating them loses the distinction between 'we are sure what this is' and 'we are sure where this is'.

revisions.change: Initial canonical publication of the Eido→Factlas observation envelope.

Additive within v1: optional `geometry` (GeoJSON extent) and `geo_anchor` (georeference provenance). Motivated by the 2026-08-03 drone-capture path audit — a property is an extent, not a point, and a consumer could not previously tell an operator-typed coordinate from telemetry-derived, model-aligned georegistration. Existing producers that send neither field are unaffected.
